entries.title: TDS on salary
entries.body: Every employer paying taxable salary to an employee must deduct TDS at the time of payment. There is no fixed rate; tax is deducted at the employee's average rate of income-tax computed on estimated salary for the year under the applicable slab (old or new regime).
entries.rate: Average rate of income-tax on estimated total salary (i.e. the employee's slab rate, including surcharge and cess as applicable). No single flat rate.
entries.rate_no_pan: Sec 206AA applies — TDS at the higher of the rate in force or 20% (in practice 20% if estimated tax works out lower), but cannot exceed the slab computation in most salary cases. CA should confirm treatment for the specific employee.
entries.threshold: No fixed monetary threshold. TDS arises only if estimated annual salary exceeds the basic exemption limit after considering eligible deductions/rebate (e.g. sec 87A rebate up to Rs 12 lakh taxable income under the new regime for FY 2025-26 onwards means many employees have nil tax).
entries.payer: Employer (any person responsible for paying salary)

sources.name: ClearTax — TDS & TCS changes from April 2026

entries.caveats: Rate depends entirely on the employee's regime choice and slab; the new tax regime (with sec 87A rebate making income up to Rs 12 lakh effectively tax-free for FY 2025-26 onwards) is now the default. IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL CHANGE: the Income-tax Act 1961 was repealed w.e.f. 01-04-2026 and replaced by the Income-tax Act 2025; salary TDS is now governed by Sec 392 (TDS challans/returns use new payment codes, not the label '192'). The label '192' is retained here only because it remains the universally-used reference. CA must confirm regime, exemption limit and rebate for the specific employee and use the correct new-Act section/code when filing.

entries.title: TDS on premature EPF withdrawal
entries.body: When the trustees of the EPF scheme (or the EPFO) pay an employee the accumulated PF balance before five years of continuous service, TDS is deducted. Applies only to taxable premature withdrawals.
entries.rate_no_pan: 20% (Sec 206AA). NOTE: the earlier 'maximum marginal rate if no PAN' rule was removed by the Finance Act 2023 (w.e.f. 01-04-2023); it is now 20%, not MMR.
entries.threshold: Rs 50,000 (aggregate taxable withdrawal in the year). No TDS if the taxable amount is below Rs 50,000.
entries.payer: Trustees of the EPF scheme / EPFO (person paying the accumulated balance)

sources.name: Studycafe — Budget 2023 192A no-PAN 20% not MMR
sources.ref: Finance Act 2023, second proviso to Sec 192A omitted

entries.caveats: No-PAN rate is 20% (not the maximum marginal rate) since 01-04-2023 — many secondary sources still incorrectly quote ~34.6% MMR; the omission of the second proviso is the correct current position. An inoperative PAN (not Aadhaar-linked) is treated as no PAN. Now mapped to Sec 392(7) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026 (rate/threshold unchanged). No TDS where Form 15G/15H is furnished or other exemptions apply.

entries.title: TDS on interest on securities
entries.body: Any person paying a resident interest on securities (e.g. debentures, government securities) must deduct TDS at the time of credit or payment, whichever is earlier.
entries.threshold: Rs 10,000 per financial year (raised from Rs 5,000 by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025). For specific securities such as 8% Savings (Taxable) Bonds / Floating Rate Savings Bonds the threshold is Rs 10,000; debentures of a listed company paid to an individual/HUF also have a Rs 10,000 limit.
entries.payer: Person paying interest on securities (company, government, etc.)
entries.caveats: General threshold raised to Rs 10,000 w.e.f. 01-04-2025 (Finance Act 2025). Several security-type-specific thresholds and exemptions exist (e.g. certain government securities, dematerialised listed securities) — CA should confirm the exact limit for the specific security. Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026.

entries.title: TDS on dividend
entries.body: An Indian company (or a company in which the public is substantially interested) paying dividend to a resident shareholder must deduct TDS before making the payment.
entries.threshold: Rs 10,000 per financial year per shareholder (raised from Rs 5,000 by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025).
entries.payer: Indian company / principal officer paying the dividend
entries.caveats: Threshold raised from Rs 5,000 to Rs 10,000 w.e.f. 01-04-2025 (Finance Act 2025). Applies to dividends paid to residents; dividends to non-residents fall under Sec 195. Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026.

entries.title: TDS on interest other than securities
entries.body: Any person (other than individual/HUF not under tax audit) paying a resident interest other than interest on securities — e.g. bank fixed-deposit interest, interest on loans — must deduct TDS at credit or payment, whichever is earlier.
entries.threshold: Where payer is a bank, co-operative society engaged in banking, or post office: Rs 50,000 per year (Rs 1,00,000 for senior citizens). In all other cases: Rs 10,000 per year. (Bank/senior thresholds raised by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025; previously Rs 40,000 / Rs 50,000.)
entries.payer: Payer of interest (banks, co-operative societies, post offices, companies, firms; individuals/HUF only if under tax audit in the preceding year)

sources.name: IndiaFilings — TDS rule changes from 1 April 2025

entries.caveats: Finance Act 2025 (w.e.f. 01-04-2025) raised bank/co-op/post-office threshold to Rs 50,000 (general) and Rs 1,00,000 (senior citizens); the 'other cases' threshold stayed Rs 10,000. No TDS where Form 15G/15H is furnished or income is below the basic exemption. Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026. CA should confirm whether the payer is a 'specified' payer (bank etc.) versus 'other', as the threshold differs.

entries.title: TDS on payments to contractors
entries.body: Any specified person paying a resident contractor/sub-contractor for carrying out any work (including supply of labour) under a contract must deduct TDS at credit or payment, whichever is earlier.
entries.rate: 1% if payee is an individual or HUF; 2% if payee is any other person (company, firm, etc.)
entries.threshold: Rs 30,000 per single contract/payment, OR Rs 1,00,000 in aggregate during the financial year. If aggregate crosses Rs 1,00,000, TDS applies on all payments including earlier sub-Rs 30,000 ones. (Aggregate limit was raised from Rs 75,000 to Rs 1,00,000 by the Finance Act 2024 w.e.f. 01-04-2025; single-payment limit unchanged at Rs 30,000.)
entries.payer: Specified persons (companies, firms, government, individuals/HUF under tax audit, etc.)
entries.caveats: Rates (1%/2%) unchanged in Budget 2025. Aggregate annual threshold is Rs 1,00,000 (raised from Rs 75,000 w.e.f. 01-04-2025); single-transaction threshold Rs 30,000. Special exemption: no TDS to a transporter (goods carriage) owning <=10 vehicles who furnishes PAN and a declaration. Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026. CA should confirm the new-Act payment code and whether 'manpower/labour supply' is treated under the new contractor sub-table (some FY 2026-27 commentary references a 1%/2% manpower-services entry that should be verified).

entries.title: TDS on insurance commission
entries.body: Any person paying a resident remuneration or reward by way of commission for soliciting or procuring insurance business must deduct TDS at credit or payment, whichever is earlier.
entries.rate: 2% if payee is a resident other than a company; 10% if payee is a domestic company. (Rate for non-company residents reduced from 5% to 2% by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025.)
entries.threshold: Rs 20,000 per financial year (raised from Rs 15,000 by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025).
entries.payer: Insurer / person paying insurance commission
entries.caveats: Two distinct effective dates: rate cut 5%->2% for non-company residents w.e.f. 01-04-2025 (Finance Act 2025); threshold raised Rs 15,000->Rs 20,000 also w.e.f. 01-04-2025. Domestic companies remain at 10%. Some charts still show a flat 5% (stale). Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026. CA should confirm the payee's status (company vs other) to pick 10% vs 2%.

Threshold: Rs 20,000 per financial year (raised from Rs 15,000 by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025). Payer: Insurer / person paying insurance commission. Payee: Resident insurance agent (commission earner). insurance commission insurance agent

entries.title: TDS on life-insurance payout
entries.body: Any person paying a resident a sum under a life-insurance policy (maturity/surrender proceeds) that is NOT exempt under sec 10(10D) must deduct TDS. Tax is on the income component only, not the gross payout.
entries.rate: 2% on the income component (payout minus total premiums paid). Reduced from 5% to 2% by the Finance Act 2024 w.e.f. 01-10-2024.
entries.threshold: Rs 1,00,000 (aggregate non-exempt payout under the policy in the financial year). No TDS if the aggregate is below Rs 1,00,000.
entries.payer: Insurer making the policy payout

sources.name: TaxGuru — Section 194DA TDS on life insurance

entries.caveats: Rate cut from 5% to 2% w.e.f. 01-10-2024 (Finance/No.2 Act 2024) — several charts still show 5% (stale). TDS is on the income portion (proceeds less premiums paid), not the gross sum. Applies only to payouts NOT exempt under sec 10(10D); fully exempt maturity proceeds are outside this section. Threshold Rs 1,00,000 is per policy aggregate in the year. Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026.

entries.title: TDS on commission or brokerage
entries.body: Any person (other than individual/HUF not under tax audit) paying a resident commission or brokerage (other than insurance commission, which is under 194D) must deduct TDS at credit or payment, whichever is earlier.
entries.rate: 2% (reduced from 5% by the Finance/No.2 Act 2024 w.e.f. 01-10-2024).
entries.threshold: Rs 20,000 per financial year (raised from Rs 15,000 by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025).
entries.payer: Person paying commission/brokerage (companies, firms, individuals/HUF under tax audit)
entries.caveats: Two effective dates: rate cut 5%->2% w.e.f. 01-10-2024; threshold raised Rs 15,000->Rs 20,000 w.e.f. 01-04-2025. Several charts still show 5% (stale — that was the pre-Oct-2024 rate). Excludes insurance commission (194D) and brokerage on securities transactions. Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026.

entries.title: TDS on rent
entries.body: Any person (other than individual/HUF not under tax audit) paying a resident rent for the use of plant/machinery/equipment, or land/building/furniture/fittings, must deduct TDS at credit or payment, whichever is earlier.
entries.rate: 2% for use of plant, machinery or equipment [sec 194-I(a)]; 10% for use of land, building (incl. factory building), furniture or fittings [sec 194-I(b)].
entries.threshold: Rs 6,00,000 per financial year (raised from Rs 2,40,000 by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025). Several sources describe it as a Rs 50,000-per-month basis, but the statutory limit is expressed as Rs 6,00,000 per year per payee.
entries.payer: Person paying rent (companies, firms, individuals/HUF under tax audit)
entries.caveats: Threshold raised from Rs 2,40,000 to Rs 6,00,000 per year w.e.f. 01-04-2025 (Finance Act 2025) — many charts (incl. some FY 2026-27 ones) still show Rs 2,40,000 (stale); this is a common error point. CA should VERIFY whether the limit is applied per-annum (Rs 6,00,000) or per-month (Rs 50,000) for borderline cases — sources phrase it both ways. Rates (2% / 10%) unchanged. Distinct from 194-IB (rent paid by small individuals/HUF). Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026.

reviewFlags: THRESHOLD BASIS: stated as Rs6,00,000/yr here; the FA2025 statutory basis is Rs50,000/MONTH (deepseek's framing). Annual vs monthly matters for part-year tenancies — CA to confirm the operative basis.

entries.title: TDS on transfer of immovable property
entries.body: Any person (transferee) buying immovable property (other than agricultural land) from a resident must deduct TDS at the time of credit or payment. Reported via Form 26QB.
entries.threshold: Consideration OR stamp-duty value of Rs 50,00,000 or more (whichever is higher). If either value is Rs 50 lakh or more, TDS applies on the higher of the two; no TDS only if BOTH are below Rs 50 lakh.
entries.payer: Transferee / buyer (any person, including individuals — no tax-audit precondition)

sources.name: Income Tax Department — TDS on purchase of immovable property
ClearTax — Section 194IA file TDS on sale of property

entries.caveats: Finance/No.2 Act 2024 (w.e.f. 01-10-2024) clarified that the 1% applies on the HIGHER of consideration or stamp-duty value, and that where there are multiple transferors/transferees the Rs 50 lakh test uses aggregate consideration. Excludes agricultural land. Buyer needs no TAN (uses Form 26QB). Under the Income-tax Act 2025, the four PAN-based forms (26QB/26QC/26QD/26QE) are consolidated into Form 141 for Tax Year 2026-27 onwards — CA should file using the new form. Sale by a non-resident falls under Sec 195, not 194-IA.

entries.title: TDS on rent paid by individuals/HUF (not under audit)
entries.body: An individual or HUF who is NOT liable to tax audit and pays rent to a resident must deduct TDS once a year (in the last month of the tenancy or the financial year). Reported via Form 26QC.
entries.rate: 2% (reduced from 5% by the Finance/No.2 Act 2024 w.e.f. 01-10-2024).
entries.rate_no_pan: 20% (Sec 206AA), capped at the rent for the last month (statutory cap to prevent over-deduction).
entries.threshold: Rent exceeding Rs 50,000 for a month or part of a month.
entries.payer: Individual / HUF tenant not subject to tax audit
entries.caveats: Rate cut from 5% to 2% w.e.f. 01-10-2024 (Finance/No.2 Act 2024) — some charts still show 5% (stale). Threshold (Rs 50,000/month) unchanged. Deduction is once per year; no TAN required (Form 26QC, consolidating into Form 141 under the Income-tax Act 2025 for Tax Year 2026-27). Distinct from 194-I (which covers larger/business payers). Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026.
entries.actNew2025: Sec 393(1) — non-salary TDS. Tentative: Sl.2(i), code 1007. Form 26QC -> Form 141.

entries.title: TDS on professional or technical services
entries.body: Any person (other than individual/HUF not under tax audit) paying a resident fees for professional services, fees for technical services, royalty, or non-compete sums must deduct TDS at credit or payment, whichever is earlier.
entries.rate: 10% in general (professional fees, royalty, non-compete). 2% for fees for technical services (FTS), royalty for sale/distribution/exhibition of cinematographic films, and payees engaged solely in the business of operating a call centre.
entries.threshold: Rs 50,000 per financial year per category (raised from Rs 30,000 by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025). The Rs 50,000 limit applies separately to each item (professional fees, FTS, royalty, sec 28(va) sums).
entries.payer: Person paying professional/technical fees (companies, firms, individuals/HUF under tax audit)
entries.caveats: Threshold raised from Rs 30,000 to Rs 50,000 (per category) w.e.f. 01-04-2025 (Finance Act 2025) — many charts still show Rs 30,000 (stale). The 2%-vs-10% split: 2% applies to FTS, film-royalty and call-centre operators; 10% to professional fees, other royalty and non-compete. Now governed by Sec 393(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026. CA should classify the payment correctly (FTS vs professional) since the rate differs.

entries.title: TDS on income from mutual-fund units
entries.body: Any person paying a resident income in respect of units of a mutual fund (specified under sec 10(23D)) or specified company/undertaking must deduct TDS. Covers dividend/income distributions on units, NOT capital gains on redemption.
entries.threshold: Rs 10,000 per financial year (raised from Rs 5,000 by the Finance Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2025).
entries.payer: Mutual fund / person paying income on units

sources.ref: Sec 194K, 10% on income from MF units

entries.title: TDS on cash withdrawals
entries.body: A bank, co-operative bank or post office must deduct TDS on cash withdrawals by a person from one or more accounts beyond the prescribed annual limit. Designed to discourage large cash dealings.
entries.rate: 2% on cash withdrawal exceeding Rs 1 crore (for persons who have filed ITR). For non-filers of ITR (all three preceding years): 2% on withdrawals between Rs 20 lakh and Rs 1 crore, and 5% above Rs 1 crore.
entries.rate_no_pan: Sec 206AA applies; 194N TDS is on the amount above the threshold. Practically the 2%/5% rates above apply (no separate PAN-less rate commonly quoted because withdrawals are from identified accounts). CA to confirm.
entries.threshold: Rs 1 crore per year (ITR filers); Rs 20 lakh per year (non-filers of ITR for all three preceding years).
entries.payer: Bank / co-operative bank / post office paying cash

entries.title: TDS by e-commerce operator
entries.body: An e-commerce operator must deduct TDS on the gross amount of sales of goods or services facilitated through its digital platform for a resident e-commerce participant, at credit or payment (incl. payment by the buyer directly to the seller), whichever is earlier.
entries.rate: 0.1% (reduced from 1% by the Finance/No.2 Act 2024 w.e.f. 01-10-2024).
entries.rate_no_pan: 5% (special higher rate under sec 206AA for 194O, not 20%).
entries.threshold: For an individual/HUF participant: gross amount up to Rs 5,00,000 in the year with PAN/Aadhaar furnished — no TDS. No threshold for other participants.
entries.payer: E-commerce operator
entries.payee: Resident e-commerce participant (seller on the platform)

entries.title: TDS on purchase of goods
entries.body: A buyer whose turnover/gross receipts exceeded Rs 10 crore in the preceding financial year must deduct TDS on purchase of goods from a resident seller, on the value exceeding Rs 50 lakh in the year.
entries.rate: 0.1% on the purchase value exceeding Rs 50 lakh in the financial year.
entries.rate_no_pan: 5% (special higher rate under sec 206AA for 194Q, not 20%).
entries.threshold: Rs 50,00,000 aggregate purchases from a seller in the financial year; buyer's preceding-year turnover must exceed Rs 10 crore.
entries.payer: Buyer with preceding-year turnover > Rs 10 crore
entries.caveats: TDS on the amount EXCEEDING Rs 50 lakh, not the whole purchase. No-PAN rate is 5%. With the abolition of TCS sec 206C(1H) on sale of goods w.e.f. 01-04-2025, the earlier 194Q-vs-206C(1H) overlap is resolved — for FY 2026-27, only 194Q applies on the buyer side. Does not apply where the transaction is already subject to TDS/TCS under another provision. Now governed by Sec 393 of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026.

entries.title: TDS on benefits or perquisites
entries.body: Any person providing a resident a benefit or perquisite (whether convertible into money or not) arising from that person's business or profession must deduct TDS on the value of the benefit. Covers free samples, sponsored trips, incentives in kind, etc.
entries.rate: 10% on the value/aggregate value of the benefit or perquisite.
entries.threshold: Rs 20,000 per financial year (aggregate value of benefits to the resident).
entries.payer: Person providing the benefit/perquisite (individuals/HUF exempt if turnover <= Rs 1 crore for business / Rs 50 lakh for profession in preceding year)
entries.caveats: Where the benefit is wholly in kind (or partly in kind and cash is insufficient), the provider must ensure the tax is paid before releasing the benefit. CBDT Circulars 12/2022 and 18/2022 give detailed guidance on valuation and exclusions (e.g. genuine sales discounts, dealer conferences) — CA should consult these. Small individual/HUF providers (below the turnover limits) are exempt. Now governed by Sec 393 of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026.

entries.title: TDS on transfer of virtual digital assets
entries.body: Any person paying a resident consideration for the transfer of a virtual digital asset (crypto, NFTs, etc.) must deduct TDS at credit or payment, whichever is earlier. Where transfers happen on an exchange, the exchange generally deducts.

entries.payer: Person paying for a VDA transfer (or the exchange facilitating it)

entries.title: TDS on partner remuneration / interest
entries.body: A partnership firm or LLP paying a partner salary, remuneration, commission, bonus or interest must deduct TDS at credit (including credit to the partner's capital account) or payment, whichever is earlier. New section introduced by the Finance/No.2 Act 2024.
entries.threshold: Rs 20,000 aggregate per partner per financial year.
entries.payer: Partnership firm / LLP

Covers salary/remuneration/commission/bonus/interest to partners, including amounts merely credited to the capital account. Does NOT apply to repayment of capital or share of profit (which is exempt under sec 10(2A)). Now governed by Sec 393 of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026. entries.title: TDS on payments to non-residents
entries.body: Any person paying a non-resident (or foreign company) any sum chargeable to tax in India (other than salary) must deduct TDS at the rates in force. A catch-all section for cross-border payments; rate depends on the nature of income and any applicable tax treaty.
entries.rate: Varies by nature of income — there is no single rate. Common 'rates in force' include 20% (royalty/FTS to non-corporate non-residents, subject to change), 10% (interest on certain foreign-currency borrowings), 12.5% (long-term capital gains, post-Budget-2024 regime), and 30%/40% on other income depending on payee — OR the beneficial DTAA rate.
entries.rate_no_pan: Sec 206AA: higher of 'rate in force' or 20%. Relief: under Rule 37BC, no-PAN 20% may not apply to certain payments (interest, royalty, FTS, capital gains, dividend) if the non-resident furnishes prescribed details (TRC, address, etc.).
entries.threshold: No monetary threshold — TDS applies on the whole sum chargeable to tax, however small.
entries.payer: Any person (resident or non-resident) making the payment

entries.caveats: GENERAL NOTE only — 195 rates are intrinsically payment-specific. The applicable rate is the lower of the Income-tax Act 'rate in force' (plus surcharge/cess) and the relevant DTAA rate (DTAA needs a valid TRC and Form 10F). Specific rates quoted here (20% royalty/FTS, 12.5% LTCG, etc.) are indicative and were themselves changed by recent Finance Acts — CA MUST verify the exact rate for the specific payment, payee residence and treaty, and consider Form 15CA/15CB compliance. Now governed by Sec 393(2) of the Income-tax Act 2025 w.e.f. 01-04-2026. Confidence set to medium because no single figure can be authoritative for this section.

entries.title: TCS on alcohol, scrap, minerals and forest produce
entries.body: A seller of specified goods — alcoholic liquor for human consumption, tendu leaves, timber/forest produce, scrap, and minerals (coal, lignite, iron ore) — must collect TCS from the buyer at the time of sale (debit or receipt, whichever is earlier).
entries.rate: For FY 2026-27 the rates were rationalised to a uniform 2% by the Finance Act 2026 (w.e.f. 01-04-2026) for alcoholic liquor, tendu leaves, scrap and minerals (coal/lignite/iron ore). Timber/forest produce was already 2% (w.e.f. 01-04-2025).
entries.rate_no_pan: Sec 206CC: higher of twice the relevant rate or 5%.
entries.threshold: No monetary threshold — TCS applies on the sale value of the specified goods (subject to the buyer-declaration exemption below).
entries.payer: Seller of the specified goods (collector)

sources.name: TaxGuru — TCS rates rationalised to uniform 2% from 1 April 2026

entries.caveats: RATES CHANGED for FY 2026-27. Pre-01-04-2026 (FY 2025-26): alcoholic liquor 1%, scrap 1%, minerals 1%, tendu leaves 5%, timber under forest lease 2%. The Finance Act 2026 made alcohol/scrap/minerals 2% (up from 1%) and tendu leaves 2% (down from 5%) w.e.f. 01-04-2026. CA should VERIFY the exact FY 2026-27 rate for timber under forest lease vs other forest produce (the primary source extracts confirmed alcohol/tendu/scrap/minerals at 2% but were less explicit on the two timber categories — one secondary chart shows timber/forest produce at 2%). No TCS where the buyer is a resident manufacturer/processor/power-generator who furnishes a declaration (Form 27C) that the goods are not for trading. Now governed by Sec 394(1) of the Income-tax Act 2025. Confidence medium pending CA confirmation of the timber line items and the Form 27C exemption.
